request.contents:
Does the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (Ontario) make this clause of a residential tenancy agreement void?

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Decide using only the sections of the Act below. They are a selection, not the whole Act.

<sections>
[The headings and text of sections 4, 14, 15, 20, 22, 25, 26, 27, 34, 37, 40, 105, 106, 108, 116, 119, 120, 134 of the Act, from e-Laws; SHA-256 170f924284b858615f0e872622e0e1150d171bcaeffe1a8e61a2ea40a42b0e8c. Left out of saved records.]
</sections>

<clause>
The Tenant's guarantor will pay the Landlord $1,000 on signing as security for the Tenant's obligations under this Agreement, to be returned when the tenancy ends.
</clause>

Answer with:
- verdict: "void" if the Act makes the clause void, "allowed" if the Act permits it, or "unsure" if these sections don't let you decide.
- section: the number of the one section that decides it, such as "14", without a subsection. Empty if unsure.
- quote: the words of that section that decide it, copied exactly: one continuous passage from a single subsection, at least five words, with nothing left out, added or changed. Not a heading. Empty if unsure.
- reason: one or two sentences.

text: {"verdict":"void","section":"105","quote":"The only security deposit that a landlord may collect is a rent deposit collected in accordance with section 106.","reason":"Money paid on a tenant's behalf by a guarantor to be held as security for the tenant's obligations and returned at the end of the tenancy is a security deposit as defined in section 105(2), not a rent deposit applied to the last rent period under section 106. Because section 105(1) prohibits collecting any security deposit other than a lawful rent deposit, this clause is inconsistent with the Act and void under section 4(1)."}

parsed.quote: The only security deposit that a landlord may collect is a rent deposit collected in accordance with section 106.
parsed.reason: Money paid on a tenant's behalf by a guarantor to be held as security for the tenant's obligations and returned at the end of the tenancy is a security deposit as defined in section 105(2), not a rent deposit applied to the last rent period under section 106. Because section 105(1) prohibits collecting any security deposit other than a lawful rent deposit, this clause is inconsistent with the Act and void under section 4(1).
